records.eligibility_reason: The programme is for 'African students and recent graduates' of 'any post-secondary institution in Africa'; neither the page nor the FAQ publishes a country list, so the DRC is not named and its position is unknown under the Africa-alone rule. 'Recent graduate' is undefined (the profile's degree dates from 2024) and the programme asks for at least 10 hours a week for eight months; no business is needed, and English, required for assignments, is among the profile's languages.
application_process: Apply online by 1 December 2026 (the Apply button on the official page opens a Queen's University Qualtrics form)
Results are announced in late December for the cohort starting in January (official FAQ)
Selection funnel: Explore (January-February), Ignite (March-April), Launch and Fellowship (May-August) for up to 60 Fellows

records.notes: 2 November 2026 (rerun, plain-curl read): label lowered from Fully Funded to Participation Funded because the organiser's page never says 'fully funded' and the stipend goes only to the final 60 Fellows; eligibility lowered from LIKELY to POSSIBLY ELIGIBLE because 'recent graduate' is undefined. 9 November 2026: page re-read; deadline (1 December 2026), funnel, stipend wording (CAD 500 and USD 350) unchanged. The page also says the programme offers downloadable content and language support for French-speaking learners. 19 November 2026 (scout D, evidence backlog): programme page and official FAQ re-read and every tracked field compared; nothing changed. The FAQ adds that accepted applicants get free access to the courses, coaches and micro-credentials, that the CAD 500 Launch-phase stipend is a seed fund for the venture, and that results come out in late December. The page still shows 'Sign up to be notified when applications launch!' next to the 'Apply By December 1, 2026' button; the button links to a Queen's Qualtrics application form, which was not opened.

records.deadline_text: Official programme page (yearly rule, no 2027-specific announcement): 'Every year, the application portal for our flagship TEF Entrepreneurship Programme opens on the 1st of January till midnight on the 1st of March at Midnight, on our digital platform, www.TEFConnect.com.'
records.eligibility_reason: The Foundation selects entrepreneurs across 'all 54 African countries', a complete set that includes the DRC, and accepts Africans aged 18 and above who reside in Africa; the profile records only an under-30 age band. Entry needs a business idea or a business under 5 years old, which the profile does not record, and the USD 5,000 seed capital is paid only after a business registration certificate, tax registration and a business bank account are submitted (the profile records no registered business).
other_requirements: To apply: a valid government-issued ID showing date of birth and photo, and a high-resolution headshot, with details matching the TEFConnect account
Before the seed capital is paid: a Business Registration Certificate, evidence of tax registration in the business name and a bank reference letter for the business account
potential_issues: Requires a business idea or a business under 5 years old
Seed capital disbursed only after document review
To receive the seed capital the business must be registered, tax-registered and have a business bank account; the profile records no registered business
The official programme page still carries the 2025 title; the 1 January to 1 March window is a yearly rule and no 2027 announcement was found on the pages read
records.notes: The official programme page still carries the 2025 title; the 1 January to 1 March window is stated as a yearly rule. 2 November 2026 (rerun): programme page re-read (window 1 January to 1 March on TEFConnect; seven phases: application, due diligence with World-Check screening and physical verification, shortlist, training, investment readiness, seed capital). Label lowered from Fully Funded to Partially Funded: the organiser describes training plus a USD 5,000 seed grant, never 'fully funded'. 19 November 2026 (scout D, evidence backlog): programme page and home page re-read and every tracked field compared; dates, funding and eligibility unchanged; deadline_text now quotes the page's exact sentence. Newly recorded: the seed capital phase requires a Business Registration Certificate, tax registration in the business name and a business bank reference letter; shortlisted applicants are notified on 22 March each year. No 2027-specific announcement on the pages read.

lead_outcomes.reason: The organiser's eligibility criteria require 'minimum 7 years' of relevant work experience' and a 'Master’s degree' ('Fellowships are open annually to young professionals, mid-career and new executives from Africa with relevant work experience and a master’s degree.'). The profile holds a Bachelor's (2024) and records under one year of internships. The 2027 call closes on 20 November 2026 ('Deadline : 20 November 2026').
The page is a blog/news reflection ('The cloud has a postcode: reflections on the CNBC Africa AI Summit 2026') about AI and data centres; it contains no call, application or programme.

Organiser's page read: 'The EAB 2027–2028 applications are now open.' and 'Applications open Closes December 13, 2026'; it targets 'physicians, engineers and entrepreneurs' for a 10-month health-technology fellowship hosted in Kigali (Rwanda) and Nairobi (Kenya). The eligibility rules (nationality/residence list, degree, profession) and any stipend are only in the call document on SharePoint, which returned HTTP 403 (call) or a Microsoft sign-in page (FAQ); no record written because the DRC position and funding could not be read.

The ILO page says the three BRMM competitions invite entrants from a closed country list that does not include the DRC: 'The International Labour Organization (ILO) has launched three competitions inviting students, researchers, journalists and media creators from Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda'. The essay competition is also for 'university students' and the profile is not enrolled. Entries close on 25 November 2026.

The DRC is not on the list. Entries close on 25 November 2026.

The organiser's eligibility criteria require a company: 'For-profit and registered in Africa', 'Management team of at least two people' and 'At least MVP, ideally recurring revenue, paying customers and established partnerships'. The profile records no registered business. The 2027 cohort deadline has also passed ('15 November 2026: Deadline to apply').

Applications closed: 'Applications close on 9 November 2026.' The programme is for higher education institutions and research centres (it asks for 'A letter from your institutional head'), not for individuals without an institution.

The organiser's 'Are you eligible?' section is for start-ups that 'Have a working technology or product (MVP or post-MVP; beyond concept stage)' ('We are looking for ambitious startups building technologies that can shape the future of snacking.'). The profile records no business or product.

The grant terms on the organiser's page: 'The Program is open to eligible startups and emerging companies building AI-driven products or services'. It gives platform credits, not cash, and 'Participant must maintain a valid payment method or other approved billing arrangement' for overage charges. The profile records no business.

The organiser's eligibility section: 'Their business must be located in one of New York City’s five boroughs.' and 'Their business has been operating for at least two years.' The profile resides in the DRC and records no business.
